columns.headline: Chad drops a monster week while Collin benches a 25-point QB
columns.dek: Chad posted the week's best score and Joe G the worst, but Collin found the most creative way to lose: starting a negative quarterback with a monster on the bench.
body: Chad scored 155.24, the high score of the week, and his best possible lineup was only 156.64. Jahmyr Gibbs carried the load and Christian Watson beat his projection of 11.52 by 17.78. Joe G was on the other side of it, and the scoreboard reads 68.26, the lowest of the week. The series between them is now tied 11-11, which tells you the last few meetings have been less polite than this one.

Joe G did not lose gracefully. CeeDee Lamb was projected for 15.46 and delivered 1.90, and RJ Harvey was good for 0.70. Justin Herbert sat on the bench with 10.24, which beat either of those starters on its own. Joe G still sits fifth at 6-4, which says something about the rest of the league.

Then there is Collin, the only loser whose best lineup would have beaten his opponent. He started Tyler Shough, who scored -0.16 against a projection of 16.51, while Jordan Love put up 25.28 on the bench. Collin's best lineup was 107.46, he lost to Jon by a final of 74.42 to 81.54, and he left 33.04 points sitting on the pine. That was also the closest game of the week, so every one of those points mattered. Collin is 2-8 and last in the standings, and the manager is the only person to blame.

Jon deserves a short lap of honor and a long look at his luck. He won with 81.54, which missed the median of 100.25, so the head-to-head win came with a median loss attached. Parker Washington scored 27.40 for him and nobody else seems to have noticed. Jon is 8-2 and sits second, behind Chad, and leads the series with Collin 4-3.

Jeff gets credit for the week's most elaborate self-sabotage that still ended in a win. Matthew Stafford started at QB and scored 0.00 against a projection of 18.17, while Mike Evans put up 22.80 and C.J. Stroud 20.94 on the bench. Jeff beat Brad anyway, 108.36 to 100.70, and jumped three spots to sixth. Brad can console himself that Isaiah Likely scored 26.90, even as Carnell Tate laid 1.10 in a slot that wanted 11.10. Brad leads the series 10-7, for whatever that is worth to him now.

The best start belonged to TJ, whose Drake Maye scored 39.46 on a projection of 18.47, and TJ beat Ben 123.56 to 99.80. Ben missed the median by a margin so thin it was a rounding error, and he fell three places to tenth. Joe K matched Jeff's climb, rising three places on a 124.88 win over Kris, even with Jeremiyah Love turning in 2.20. Jared fell three places after Flanders beat him 96.34 to 85.92, and Flanders celebrated by climbing out of last place into 11th, a promotion nobody wants.
